newsitem.title: CHINA: China says Dalai Lama a "splittist" in Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China says Dalai Lama a "splittist" in Taiwan.

text.p: China lashed out at Tibet's exiled spiritual leader the Dalai Lama on Thursday, saying his visit to Taiwan was a bid to engage in "splittist" activities.
"The Dalai Lama has for a long time been engaged around the world in activities to split the motherland," Foreign Ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said.
"This time he has run to Taiwan, apparently bringing along his political goals," Cui told a regular news briefing.

The Dalai Lama on Thursday wrapped up a six-day visit to Taiwan by meeting Taiwanese President Lee Teng-hui and calling for the Nationalist-ruled island to find a compromise with the communist mainland.

"We are opposed to any person using any methods in any place to engage in activities to split the motherland or disrupt ethnic unity," Cui said when asked to comment on the meeting between the Dalai Lama and Lee.
Beijing regularly accuses the Dalai Lama of working for independence for Tibet and has blasted his Taiwan visit as a splittist crusade.
"Why have a small number of people on Taiwan island been so eager to pander to these activities of his? We must ask this question," Cui said.
Communist Beijing has regarded Taiwan as a rebel-held province since the Nationalist army fled there in 1949 at the end of the Chinese civil war.
Beijing says Taipei is paying only lip service to pledges of reunification and suspects the island's leadership of secretly seeking to set up an independent state.
"Taiwan and Tibet are inseparable parts of China," Cui said. "Defending ethnic unity and realising the unification of the motherland are the common wishes of the entire Chinese people."
"Anyone who moves against the tide of history will not achieve success," he said.

The globe-trotting Buddhist leader denies he wants to split Tibet from China but has led a non-violent campaign for more autonomy for his Himalayan homeland under Chinese sovereignty, for which he won the 1989 Nobel Peace Prize.
